title: Add AsyncKeyStore API for async PostgreSQL backend (asyncpg)
description: Add an async API surface to support a Postgres backend implemented with asyncpg without forcing sync callers into event loop management.
design:
Introduce an async-first keystore API to support async PostgreSQL drivers (asyncpg).

Design sketch:
- Add AsyncKeyStore (or a parallel API surface) with equivalent operations needed for DB-backed keystore behavior.
- Keep existing KeyStore synchronous and defaulting to SQLite (backwards compatibility).
- AsyncKeyStore should accept the same path concept but use env config to select backend; for postgres it uses asyncpg.
- Provide minimal shared business logic between KeyStore and AsyncKeyStore where feasible.

Notes:
- Avoid calling asyncio.run inside library methods (breaks callers running inside event loops).
- Consider a small adapter layer so common DB operations are implemented once per backend.
acceptance_criteria:
- AsyncKeyStore exists and can be instantiated.
- AsyncKeyStore uses asyncpg when configured for Postgres.
- Basic CRUD operations are available asynchronously (initially: connect/init schema + simple sanity op).
- Existing synchronous KeyStore remains unchanged for SQLite users.
notes: Unblocked after epic rescope: Postgres support will be delivered via AsyncKeyStore (asyncpg) directly; proceeding with implementation under 82j.
close_reason: Completed: AsyncKeyStore exists, uses asyncpg, supports schema init/ensure + basic read/write; import_key + full read parity implemented; tests cover backend and parity. Closing parent to unblock dependent tasks.

title: AsyncKeyStore/AsyncPgBackend: implement import_key and full schema writes
description:
Implement AsyncKeyStore.import_key(...) mirroring sync KeyStore.import_key semantics.

Requirements:
- Read cert bytes from file
- Use existing parse_cert_file/parse_cert_bytes to extract uids/subkeys/certs
- Persist full schema in Postgres via AsyncPgBackend (keys, subkeys, uidvalues, uidemails/uidnames/uiduris, uidcerts, uidcertlist)
- Return a Key object equivalent to sync get_key result

This enables backend contract tests to share the same test data fixtures across sync+async backends.
notes: Implementation done and pushed (AsyncKeyStore.import_key + AsyncPgBackend.save_full_key + integration test). Beads won't allow closing while 19e is open; consider removing dependency or close later when 19e is completed.
close_reason: Completed: import_key + full schema writes implemented and tested; used by 19e parity work.

title: Implement PostgreSQL backend (asyncpg) for AsyncKeyStore
description: Rescope: Provide PostgreSQL persistence support via the async API (AsyncKeyStore) using asyncpg. Keep the existing synchronous KeyStore SQLite-only to avoid event-loop bridging. The epic is now focused on: asyncpg connection + schema init + minimal keystore operations + tests, plus wiring so backend selection via env works for AsyncKeyStore.
design:
Add a PostgreSQL backend alongside the existing SQLite backend.

Key considerations:
- Abstract DB operations behind a backend interface (connect, migrations/schema init, CRUD primitives used by the library).
- Configuration: support selecting backend via env var / config file / connection string.
- SQL compatibility: adjust queries for Postgres (parameter placeholders, returning clauses, UPSERT syntax, foreign keys, etc.).
- Migrations: either maintain neutral migrations or backend-specific; ensure initial schema can be created in Postgres.
- Connection/pooling: use a robust driver (likely psycopg/psycopg2) with pooling and proper transaction handling.
- Testing: run backend contract tests against both SQLite and Postgres; add CI service container for Postgres.

Out of scope (initial epic): performance tuning, advanced pooling, multi-tenant schemas.
acceptance_criteria:
- PostgreSQL backend is available via AsyncKeyStore using asyncpg.
- Schema is created/initialized successfully on a fresh Postgres database.
- Core keystore operations needed by AsyncKeyStore work end-to-end on Postgres (initial scope: schema init + minimal read/write proof: save_key_info + list_fingerprints).
- Existing synchronous KeyStore remains SQLite-only (no event loop bridging).
- Automated tests cover the async Postgres backend behavior (schema + minimal CRUD proof).
notes: Rescoped: implement Postgres backend via asyncpg for AsyncKeyStore; do not add sync Postgres backend behind KeyStore. This unblocks async work without event loop bridging.
close_reason: Completed: AsyncPgBackend + AsyncKeyStore provide asyncpg Postgres support including schema init/ensure, import_key with full schema writes, and full Key reconstruction; integration tests cover behavior.

title: mypy reports 'Duplicate module named "smartcards"' due to conflicting files
description:
Running mypy on the project results in the following error:

smartcardtests/smartcards.py: error: Duplicate module named "smartcards" (also at "./sm2/smartcards.py")
smartcardtests/smartcards.py: note: See https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/running_mypy.html#mapping-file-paths-to-modules for more info
smartcardtests/smartcards.py: note: Common resolutions include: a) using `--exclude` to avoid checking one of them, b) adding `__init__.py` somewhere, c) using `--explicit-package-bases` or adjusting MYPYPATH
Found 1 error in 1 file (errors prevented further checking)

This is likely caused by having two files named 'smartcards.py' in different directories ('smartcardtests/' and 'sm2/'), which confuses mypy's module resolution. See the linked mypy documentation for possible solutions.
